lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: There it is, the proverb exactly: the fawn hunting the lion.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: What are you so worked up about, Cnemon?

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: You ask what I’m worked up about? I’ve been outsmarted, miserable idiot that I am, and left an heir I never meant to have—passing over the very people I’d most have wanted to get my estate.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: I was cultivating Hermolaus—the very rich one, no children, expected dead any minute—and he was not at all offended by the attention. So I thought this would be clever: make a public will leaving him everything I owned, so he’d copy me out of rivalry and do the same.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: What he wrote in his own will, I do not know. I, at any rate, suddenly died when the roof fell in on me. And now Hermolaus has my property—like a sea-bass that swallowed the hook along with the bait.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Not just the hook. You too, the fisherman. So you set up a clever little trap for yourself.

lines.speaker: Cnemon
lines.text: Apparently. Which is why I’m howling.
